1.title: The Quality Practice
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: The Quality Practice. It covers the exam area The prince two practices. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Explain the purpose of the quality practice and its relationships with the principles. Explain the purpose of the product description, quality management approach, quality register and product register. Define user quality expectations, acceptance criteria, quality specifications and requirements. Describe quality planning, quality control and quality assurance. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two practices (sixty percent). Exam format: sixty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; thirty-six correct answers (sixty percent) pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Foundation syllabus (people cert).

1.title: Purpose
1.text: Purpose. The quality practice defines and implements the means by which the project will create products that are fit for purpose: products that meet user needs and can be accepted. It supports focus on products.

1.title: Key concepts
1.text: Key concepts. User quality expectations. What the users expect of the product's quality. Acceptance criteria. The measurable conditions a product must meet to be accepted. Quality specifications. The detailed measures (standards, tolerances) the product must meet. Requirements. What the product must do or provide (needs, features). Exam tip: Expectations come from users; acceptance criteria say how acceptance is judged; specifications give the detailed measures. All are agreed before work starts.

1.title: Quality planning, control and assurance
1.text: Quality planning, control and assurance. The figure shows this: Quality planning, quality control and quality assurance.

1.title: Quality planning, control and assurance, continued
1.text: Quality planning, control and assurance. Quality planning. Meaning: Decide how quality will be achieved: standards, criteria, methods, responsibilities. Who: Project manager with the team and assurance input. Quality control. Meaning: Check products against their criteria (tests, reviews, inspections) and record results. Who: The team producing and checking the work.

1.title: Quality planning, control and assurance, continued
1.text: Quality planning, control and assurance. Quality assurance. Meaning: Independent assessment that the quality processes are working and the project is on track to meet needs. Who: Project assurance or an independent function. Exam tip: Control checks the product. Assurance checks the system and the process. If the checker is independent of the team, think assurance.

1.title: Management products
1.text: Management products. Product description. Describes a product's purpose, composition, derivation, format and quality criteria, plus how quality will be checked. Quality management approach (P I D). How quality will be achieved on the project. Quality register (project log). A record of all quality checks planned and done, and their results. Product register (project log). A record of the products, their status and approval. Exam tip: Acceptance criteria, user quality expectations and quality specifications are agreed before the product is built, not after.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A tester runs a set of checks on a delivered component and records the results. Which activity is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Quality control. Checking products against criteria is quality control.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which statements are C O R R E C T? (one) Quality control checks products against their criteria. (two) Quality assurance independently assesses whether quality processes work. (three) Quality planning happens only after delivery. (four) Quality assurance is carried out by the team that builds the product. The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: one and two. Control checks products; assurance independently assesses the quality system.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Identify the missing word. blank are the measurable conditions a product must meet to be accepted. The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Acceptance criteria. That is the definition of acceptance criteria.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which register records every planned and completed quality check with its results? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Quality register. The quality register records quality checks and results.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which document describes a product's purpose, composition and quality criteria? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Product description. That is a product description.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which principle does the quality practice most directly support? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Focus on products. Quality starts from defining products and their criteria.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the purpose of the quality practice? Answer: To create products that are fit for purpose. Question two. Define acceptance criteria. Answer: The measurable conditions a product must meet to be accepted. Question three. Which activity checks products against their criteria? Answer: Quality control.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which activity is an independent assessment of the quality processes? Answer: Quality assurance. Question five. What does the product register record? Answer: The products, their status and approval. Question six. Where is the quality approach recorded? Answer: In the quality management approach, part of the P I D.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Purpose: create products that are fit for purpose. Concepts: user quality expectations, acceptance criteria, quality specifications, requirements. Activities: planning (decide), control (check product), assurance (independent check of the system). Products: product description, quality management approach, quality register, product register.
